summary: Implemented the MCP internal API-key boundary: constant-time key middleware applied to all 15 protected routes, production startup fails when MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY is absent/empty, and route-level tests for missing/invalid/valid keys. Could not run cargo to verify because the tool policy blocks it.
follow_up: In dev the internal API is now fail-closed when MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY is unset (previously it accepted any key); dev workflows relying on the open boundary must set the key to match the MCP server's.
Consider adding MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY to .env.example for dev.
important_context: The tool policy blocks cargo/make/sh/helm, so the Rust changes were not compiled or test-run; verify in an environment where cargo is permitted (e.g. `make backend-check backend-test`).

NetworkPolicy requirement already satisfied by existing manifests: core allows ingress from the traefik namespace and MCP calls core via the public HTTPS origin (https://cal.hajnal.space) through traefik; TLS retained on the public service path. No manifest change was needed.
